Subject: Operational Radar & OKR Triage — QBR prep

Team — sending a compact readout for this week as we lock the QBR narrative. I focused the note on wins that matter for leadership, immediate risks we should surface, and concrete asks (owners + timing). Short and actionable so we can lift into the QBR slides.

Wins
- Dedicated rollout: 3-prod clusters are green after the zonal failover test (throughput within 6% of baseline). Ops and Runtime confirmed metrics.
- Customer expansion: Acme PoC signaled readiness to move from pilot to proof-of-value (see Joel’s note below). Potential +$320k ARR if procurement clears.
- Eval regressions: Auto-eval pipeline flagged only 1 minor drift issue (tokenization mismatch), fix landed and will be validated today.

Risks / Open Concerns
- Capacity lanes: Dedicated autoscale policy is misfiring under spike patterns; we risk transient 95th percentile latency breaches if traffic repeats. (Owner: Karthik, ETA: EOD Wed)
- Contract timing: Acme legal requested a data-retention carve-out that may delay signature by 2–3 weeks. (Owner: Laura, asking leadership awareness)
- QBR narrative: We lack a concise cost-efficiency delta slide that ties batching/quantization changes to $/1M tokens. Need a short model. (Owner: Marissa + Runtime, ETA: Thu)

Asks (clear next steps)
1) Karthik: triage autoscale logs and propose two mitigations (config + short-term capacity bump). Due: 2026-12-08 17:00 PT.
2) Laura: escalate the Acme retention ask with Legal and confirm whether we can offer a guarded exception or an alternative (SLA appendix). Quick update by EOD Wed.
3) Marissa: produce the one-slide cost delta (include numbers and recommended roll-forward) for QBR deck by Thu morning.
4) Jonas: please review the attached risk matrix and add any top-3 items we should escalate to the exec QBR.

Attachments: QBR_Prep_Priorities_v2.pdf (slide deck stub), enterprise-risk-matrix.xlsx (working doc)

Thanks — will consolidate inputs into the QBR master after Thursday standup.

--
Priyom Das
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
